item.title: America 250: Colonial Games — Sun Aug 2, 2:00 PM — Weymouth Woods Sandhills Nature Preserve
item.description:
Step back in time and discover the fun of colonial games that children and families enjoyed during early American history! We will have interactive games for you to learn and play!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Shelln' Sundays — Sun Aug 2, 2:00 PM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Shell'n Sundays: Join us on Bear Island to learn about the common and uncommon treasures you may find while beachcombing along North Carolina's coast. Meet at the Bear Island Concession Stand. Note: A ferry ticket is required to attend.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Moth to Flame — Sun Aug 2, 8:00 PM — Lake Norman State Park
item.description:
What kind of bug is flying into the light by your house at night? Come to the Woodduck shelter to find out! A Ranger will be out there to see what different species of insects are attracted to lights at night.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Escape at the Millpond — Mon Aug 3 — Merchants Millpond State Park
item.description:
Come celebrate A250 with us by unlocking clues from the region's history here at Merchants Millpond! We have designed an escape room with a series of puzzles and riddles that lead you through the history of the region and NC State Parks. You will have 45 minutes to solve the clues to create a timeline of the area's history and secure the key to escape. Registration is required for this program. To sign up for a time please call 252-357-1191. Gather your friends or family (max. 10 people) if you are up for the challenge.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: NCMA Online Course for Educators: Art and Literacy — Mon Aug 3
item.description:
This self-paced course runs from Tuesday, June 16 to Tuesday, August 11. Participants can start any time between June 16 and August 4.
How can art be used to develop student growth in literacy skills? This self-paced online course explores methods for integrating art and literacy strategies to support North Carolina’s Literacy Instruction Standards across classrooms. Participants gain an understanding of how literacy is defined through a variety of lenses and apply their learning by developing a lesson plan. Strategies that incorporate NCMA works of art are used to practice and apply activities to build interpretive and expressive modes of literacy focused on a variety of reading materials, comprehension, vocabulary building, and writing. This course is designed for teachers of all disciplines and audiences. A certificate of participation for 20 hours will be provided for literacy, general, or content area credits (2 CEU, with prior approval from the local school system).
Source: NC

item.title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt — Mon Aug 3, 7:00 AM — Elk Knob State Park
item.description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks.
The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.
This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit

item.title: World Ranger Day, Storywalk © — Mon Aug 3, 8:30 AM — Chimney Rock State Park - Chimney Rock Access
item.description:
Around the globe, park rangers are on the front line in the fight to protect our natural heritage. World Ranger Day offers a chance to support their vital work, which ranges from environmental campaigning to education. The date, July 31st every year is also an opportunity to pay tribute to rangers who have lost their lives in the line of duty.
Honor and understand the duties of your North Carolina state park rangers by reading a storywalk of What a Ranger Does by Joseph Hiatt along the Great Woodland Adventure Trail.
***This event is free with paid admission to the Chimney Rock Attraction.***
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Ranger Alan's Clever Camouflage — Mon Aug 3, 10:00 AM — Merchants Millpond State Park
item.description:
Its that time of year again! Come celebrate the summer at Merchants Millpond State Park with our 4th year of the Summer Junior Adventure Series! In this series, we have a different topic that we teach about every Monday at 10 AM throughout the summer.
This week we'll talk about animals and their camouflage! We know that animals come in all different colors, but this often correlates with their environment. For most animals, the best way to stay safe is to never be seen at all! Whether its hiding from predators or setting up an ambush, camouflage plays an important role in the animal kingdom, so come out to the Millpond and learn about some of our creatures and their clever camouflage!
This program is for all ages. We will begin promptly at 10 AM at the visitor center. Guests are encouraged to dress for the weather as some of this program may be outside.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Tue Aug 4 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Spy Training 101: Decode a Secret Message — Tue Aug 4 — North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
item.description:
Pretend you’ve been recruited as a member of the Culper Spy Ring, and you need to know how to decipher a message written in invisible ink. Supplies include a paint brush, water, drying cloth, vitriol (diluted sulfuric acid), Thomas Jefferson cipher and “furnace box.” Read the clues to find the coin with a hidden message, reveal the message using the brush and vitriol, then use the cipher to decode the message.
Contact: Nancy Locquet Absillis, nancy.locquet@naturalsciences.org
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Native Plant Gardens Volunteer Day - NC the Beautiful — Tue Aug 4, 9:00 AM — Gorges State Park - Grassy Ridge Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Located at the Park’s Visitor Center, the newly established Native Landscape Garden's mission is to teach visitors to the park about native plants and their importance as well as the native pollinator species that rely on them. On the first Tuesday of each month, beginning July 7 and continuing through November 3, join Park Rangers to perform maintenance on the gardens so they continue to serve as a living native plant education opportunity to all who view them. Bring work gloves, water, hats and weather-appropriate clothing. Volunteers will receive a Friends of Gorges State Park Volunteer T-Shirt. For more information or to sign up, go to https://www.signupgenius.com/go/10C0B4CAAAC28A5FAC25-64387146-native
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Tue Aug 4, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Tue Aug 4, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Owl Appreciation Day — Tue Aug 4, 10:00 AM — Pilot Mountain State Park
item.description:
Come out to celebrate Owl appreciation day on the mountain! Park staff will have a hands-on owl education table set-up on the mountain, and we will be sharing information on what owls live in the area, how to find them, and what makes them so amazing! Want to see if you're as strong as a great horned owl? Learn the perfect barred owl call? Feel real feathers? Pop over for a hootin' good time! This event is weather permitting sadly and in the event of rain it will be canceled.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Staying Alive — Tue Aug 4, 10:00 AM — North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
item.description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026
In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.
Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.
Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.
Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Jockey's Ridge State Park — Tue Aug 4, 11:00 AM — Graveyard of the Atlantic Museum
item.description:
Join N.C. Park Ranger Austin Paul to learn about Jockeys Ridge State Park, home to the tallest living sand dune system on the Atlantic coast.
The presentation is part of the museum’s Salty Dawg Speaker Series, which features presentations on North Carolina maritime history and culture. The series is free and open to the public and is sponsored by the Friends of the Graveyard of the Atlantic Museum. Reservations are not required. Call 252-986-0720 for more information.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Schools in Parks — Tue Aug 4, 1:00 PM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:
Schools in Parks: Are you an elementary teacher working with students in grades 3–5 (homeroom, STEM, PE, art, AIG, EC, music, media coordinator, guidance counselor, etc.)? If so, come to the park to learn about the Schools in Parks program. This statewide collaboration between state parks and public schools creates outdoor learning experiences on school campuses and provides tailor-made field trips that are reimbursed. Did we mention that stipends are available for attending workshops and field trips if you are accepted into the program? Plus, you'll earn CEUs and Environmental Education credits! Meet in the Visitor Center auditorium to learn how you may qualify for this partnership.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Scales, Skins and Skeletons — Tue Aug 4, 5:00 PM — Eno River State Park - Fews Ford Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Have you ever wanted to pet a wild animal? You're in luck! Join us for the Ranger led program and learn about the different animals of the Eno, and get the chance to handle their skins, scales and skeletons!
All children must be accompanied by an adult and bring water!
Spaces are limited, and registration is required. To sign up, call (984) 250-1370 or email eno.river@ncparks.gov. Include the number of guests in your party and a phone number where you can be reached if the event is changed or canceled.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Summer Grief Photo Club (Virtual) — Tue Aug 4, 6:00 PM — Transitions LifeCare
item.description:
Adults and teens are welcome to join us for this expressive arts experience designed to explore grief through a camera lens on your own timeline. Facilitators will send participants a photography and writing prompt each week during the months of June and July. We will invite participants to complete the prompts independently and offer a virtual gathering to share our photos together. No art experience is needed. Registration is limited, please call 919-719-7199 to reserve your space.
Source: Transitions LifeCare

item.title: Knowing the West — Wed Aug 5 — North Carolina Museum of Art
item.description:
May 2–August 9, 2026
East Building, Level B, Meymandi Exhibition Gallery
Knowing the West embraces and reexamines perceptions of the American West to create more inclusive and complex dialogues. The exhibition reflects the diverse perspectives that have contributed to art and life in the region. Presenting Native American works together with art by non-Native makers, it reveals how the stories we tell and the visual language we employ influence understanding of our nation’s history and cultures.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: History for Lunch: Searching for Shell Castle: Exploring Submerged Histories on the North Carolina Coast — Wed Aug 5, 12:00 PM — Museum of the Albemarle
item.description:
Anne Mitchell Whisnant, PhD, director of graduate liberal studies at Duke University, will introduce the history of Shell Castle Island. The island was a bustling site of homes and wharves from the 1780s to the 1810s. It served as a transfer point for cargo shipping in and out of coastal North Carolina through Ocracoke Inlet. North Carolina merchant John Gray Blount and Portsmouth pilot John Wallace owned and developed Shell Island, which was worked by dozens of African American people they enslaved. At its height, Shell Castle boasted numerous buildings, enterprises, and even a lighthouse. The owners marketed it internationally with 19th-century “swag”: creamware pitchers embossed with an image of the community—one of which is on display at the museum.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Aug 6 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Thu Aug 6, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!

Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.

item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Fri Aug 7, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Fri Aug 7, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Staying Alive — Fri Aug 7, 10:00 AM — North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
item.description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026
In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.
Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.
Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.
Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

item.title: Race to the Dan: NC's Route to Victory in the Revolution — Fri Aug 7, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Dive into the untold stories and complex strategies that led North Carolina to win big in the Revolution! In 1781, North Carolina became critical to the fight for Independence. The patriot Continental Army was led by brilliant Commissioned Officers such as Nathanael Greene, Daniel Morgan, Light Horse Harry Lee, William Washington, and John Eager Howard, who came from other states to fight in the Carolinas at the head of highly trained Continental infantry and cavalry and brave southern militia. They outfought and outmaneuvered the British Army for two critical months from mid-January to mid-March and achieved a vital link to the British surrender at Yorktown six months later.
